intro.text: Welcome to the guided tour of the Media Library!

steps.text: The Media Library is accessible directly from the **navigation of the admin panel**.
The Media Library displays the **folders** that contain other folders and/or assets.
It also displays the **assets** that are not in any of the folders shown above.
**Folders** are also accessible as a tree view in the left sidebar.
A variety of buttons and options are available in the Media Library to help you manage your folders & assets. Let's discover them!
From these buttons, you can **Filter** the folders and assets, or **Search** for a specific folder or asset.
The **New** button in the top right corner allows you to **create a new folder** or **add a new asset** to the Media Library.

And from these buttons, you can respectively:
• **sort** the folder and assets.
• **switch from grid to list view**
Now that we've explored the interface, let's try managing assets and folders!
Clicking the three dots button on an asset will automatically display other buttons. Let's try it!
We can now see that for the selected asset, many actions are available, including *Download media, Move to folder*, and *Delete.*
Let's select the other asset that's not in the right folder yet.
Let's click the *Move to folder* button.
In the dialog, let's click the dropdown to reveal the list of folders.
Select 'Brand assets' from the list to move the elements to that location.
Confirm the action by clicking the *Move* button.

Our asset has been moved to the "Brand assets" folder!

Now let's add a new asset!
Before adding the new asset, let's create a new folder.
Click 'New folder' to create a new directory for your files.
We will name the new folder "PDF".
Click the *Create folder* button.
Let's go in our new "PDF" folder.

Since the folder is empty, an *Add assets* button is displayed. Let's click it!

You'll have to select a file to upload from your computer.
We can follow the upload progress in a dialog in the bottom right corner of the user interface.
Click the *Minimize* button to hide upload progress details…
… or click the *Maximize* icon to view again the full details.
Once you've uploaded a file from your computer, you can see it in the folder.
We can also add another file from your computer by dragging and dropping it.
And finally you could also add another asset from the *New* dropdown…

… by clicking on *File upload.*

Note that you can also upload a file from a URL.

Now let's learn how to manage individual assets!

Click an asset…
A details panel opens on the right side of the interface.

In the asset edition dialog, you can use the following options:
• **File name** to rename the asset
• **Location** to move the asset to another folder
• **Caption** for the asset
• **Alternative text** in case the asset isn't shown

Via the asset edition dialog, you can also use these buttons to, respectively:
• **Delete** the asset
• **Copy the link** to the asset
• **Download** the asset
• **Replace** the asset
Images can also be cropped by clicking the **Crop** button in the top right corner of their preview. Let's try it!
We can drag and drop handles in the corners of the image, or use numeric values to crop the image.
The link button helps you lock the aspect ratio.
We can also drag the circle to define the focal point. This keeps the most important part of an image visible when your front end crops or resizes it.
Let's click *Cancel* to close the cropping UI.
Click the 'Close' button to hide the details panel.
We can also select multiple assets to perform bulk actions on them.
Check the box in the upper left corner to select a first file…
… then select a second one.

When several assets are selected, a bulk actions bar is displayed.

You can use it to:
• **Select all** assets and folders
• Automatically **Create metadata** with AI (requires a Growth plan)
• **Move** selected assets to another folder
• **Delete** selected files and folders
Selected files can also moved by dragging and dropping them on any folder in the tree view.
Click the close icon to dismiss the bulk actions toolbar.

outro.text:
And that's it!

We've explored the Media Library and saw how to add and manage assets and folders ✨
